items.title: 삼성바이오 노조, 6일부로 2차 파업 돌입

items.title: SK, SK에코플랜트 상장 대신 완전 자회사화 추진
items.snippet: SK그룹 지주사 SK주식회사가 SK에코플랜트의 상장 계획을 접고 완전 자회사화를 추진한다. 지난 7월까지 마치기로 했던 기업공개(IPO)가 무산되면서 재무적투자자(FI) 보유 지분을 사들인 데 이어 소수주주 지분도 매입한다. items.title: 큐알티, 반도체 신뢰성 평가 사업 우주·유리기판으로 확대

items.title: AMD "라이젠 AI, RTX 스파크 대비 게이밍 성능·전력·가격 앞서"
items.snippet: AMD가 자사 인공지능(AI) PC의 게이밍 효율성이 경쟁사 대비 뛰어나다고 강조했다. 국내 기업과 협력해 달성한 AI 최적화 성과도 공개했다.알렉세이 나볼로킨 AMD 아시아태평양(APAC) 커머셜 영업 담당 선임 디렉터는 4일 삼성동 웨스틴 서울 파르나스에서 열린 AMD 어드밴싱 AI 서울 2026 행사에서 "여러 벤치마크 테스트를 실시한 결과 중앙처리장치(CPU)의 게이밍 성능은 AMD 제품이 엔비디아 RTX 스파크 대비 14% 우수했다"며 "게임 플레이시 배터리 사용 시간도 거의 50% 더 길게 유지됐다"고 밝혔다.CPU는 시

items.title: 모빌린트 NPU, AI 소프트웨어 '레이' 지원 개선
items.snippet: 반도체 설계(팹리스) 기업 모빌린트는 레이(Ray)에서 자사 신경망처리장치(NPU)가 자동 인식되도록 개선했다고 4일 밝혔다.레이는 대규모 AI 연산을 효율적으로 처리할 수 있도록 돕는 개방형 소프트웨어 틀(프레임워크)이다. 여러 서버와 인공지능(AI) 반도체를 연결해 연산 능력을 통합해 활용하는 방식이다.모빌린트는 한국전자통신연구원(ETRI)과 협력해 레이에서 자사 NPU가 자동 인식되고 연산 자원 할당도 지원하는 기능을 개발했다. 기존에는 모빌린트 NPU를 레이에서 활용하려면 개발자가 직접 처리장치를 별도 등록하는 등 복잡한 과

items.title: 도쿄일렉트론코리아 노태우 대표, '외국기업의 날' 동탑산업훈장 수상

items.title: 비씨엔씨, 상장 후 분기 매출 첫 300억원 돌파

items.title: 케이씨텍, 3분기 영업익 202억원...전년비 35.8% 증가
items.snippet: 케이씨텍이 올해 3분기 반도체 장비 매출 증가로 전체 매출과 영업이익이 모두 지난해보다 성장했다.케이씨텍은 올 3분기 매출 약 1142억원, 영업이익 약 202억원으로 집계됐다고 4일 공시했다. 각각 전년 동기 대비 19%, 35.8% 올랐다.주요 고객사의 반도체 생산능력 확대가 케이씨텍 올 3분기 실적을 견인했다. 회사는 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스 등에 반도체 장비를 공급한다. 반도체 소재 사업 매출은 전분기와 유사한 수준이라고 회사는 설명했다.케이씨텍 관계자는 "올 3분기는 화학기계연마(CMP) 장비 매출이 높았다"고 밝혔다. 올

items.snippet: 선익시스템이 내년 글로벌 디스플레이 장비업체 가운데 매출 1위에 오를 것이란 전망이 나왔다. 국내 장비업체가 세계 디스플레이 장비 매출 1위를 차지하는 것은 처음이다.4일 시장조사업체 카운터포인트리서치에 따르면 선익시스템은 2027년 디스플레이 장비 매출 기준 세계 1위를 기록할 것으로 예상된다.글로벌 디스플레이 장비 시장은 그동안 일본 캐논 계열과 미국 어플라이드머티어리얼즈(AMAT) 등 일본, 미국 업체가 주도해왔다. 유기발광다이오드(OLED) 증착장비 시장에서는 캐논 계열사인 캐논토키가 오랫동안 강세를 보였다. 카운터포인트는

items.title: 한진칼, 최대주주 호반건설로 변경…변수는 조원태 회장 지분 매입

items.title: 포스코퓨처엠, 회사채 수요예측에 4천500억원…전 만기 민평 밑돌아

items.title: 美 반도체 소재 기업 그린트위드, '외국기업의 날' 장관표창 수상

items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 3일 청와대에서 주재한 국무회의에서 수도권 부동산 시장과 관련해 “주요 지역들의 실제 거래 가격이 계속 떨어지고 있다. 그것도 놀라울 정도로 떨어지고 있다”며 “폭락을 걱정하는 쪽도 생겨나고 있다”고 밝혔다. 최근 서울 강남 3구(강남구, 서초구, 송파구)의 아파트 매매가격이 지속적으로 하락한 데 따른 발언으로 해석된다. 하지만 서울 전체 아파트 매매가격은 10월 넷째 주까지 90주 연속 상승했고, 하락 거래 사례는 강남권 재건축 단지 등 고가 아파트에 집중돼 있어 정확한 시장 진단이 필요하다는 지적이 나온다. ● “서울 아파트 매물 증가” 맞지만 지역별 편차 커이 대통령은 이날 국무회의에서 “예를 든다면 서울 지역의 아파트 매물이 급속도로 늘어나고 있지 않냐”며 “그리고 거래량은 매우 급속도로 줄어들고 있다”고 했다. 실제로...

items.title: 오세훈-한동훈 30분 간격 토론회, 각각 의원 38명-19명 참석
items.snippet: 오세훈 서울시장의 항소심 무죄 판결 이후 보수 야권의 차기 주도권을 둘러싼 경쟁이 시작된 가운데, 오 시장과 무소속 한동훈 의원이 같은 날 토론회를 열어 존재감 부각에 나섰다. 현역 의원 수십 명이 토론회에 몰려들고, 연임 도전 가능성이 거론되는 국민의힘 장동혁 대표도 내년도 예산안 관련 공개 일정을 소화하면서 세 대결이 본격화됐다는 해석도 나왔다.오 시장은 3일 오전 10시 서울 여의도 국회 의원회관에서 서울시와 국민의힘 서울시당이 공동 주최한 ‘세계유산 보존과 도시의 미래, 공존의 길을 찾다’ 토론회에 참석했다. 지난달 23일 여론조사비 대납 의혹 사건 항소심에서 무죄를 선고받은 이후 처음으로 국회를 찾은 것. 토론회에는 장 대표와 정점식 원내대표 등 지도부와 권영세 나경원 박충권 의원 등 현역 의원 38명이 참석했다. 오 시장은 이날도...

items.title: 靑 “전작권 전환, 조건 넘어서는 합의 가능”
items.snippet: 청와대가 3일 전시작전통제권 전환 문제와 관련해 “변화는 불가피한 상태”라며 “조건을 넘어서는 합의가 될 수 있다고 본다”고 밝혔다. 한미 군 당국 간 전작권 전환 조건 충족 여부를 두고 이견이 해소되지 않는 상황에서 조건 달성 전 특정 시점에 전작권 전환에 대한 합의가 이뤄질 수 있다고 시사한 것. 강건작 국가안보실 1차장은 이날 한 방송에서 “(제이비어) 브런슨 (주한미군)사령관은 조건을 따져야 되는 사령관이니 그 부분을 계속 강조해서 말씀하는 것”이라며 “그런데 전작권 전환을 위한 전체적인 평가는 미국과 함께 전략적, 상황적 평가 이런 것을 해 나가면 사실 조건을 넘어서는 어떤 합의가 될 수 있다고 본다”고 말했다. 최근 브런슨 사령관이 북한 위협과 안보 환경 변화로 인한 ‘새로운 기준’을 언급하고 조건 충족 필요성을 강조해 왔다. 강...

items.title: “韓-튀르키예 원전 금융 협력, 방산 공동생산도 확대”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령은 3일 국빈 방한한 레제프 타이이프 에르도안 튀르키예 대통령과 정상회담을 갖고 원전·방산·인프라 등 전략 분야에서 실질 협력을 더욱 내실화하기로 뜻을 모았다. 이 대통령은 이날 청와대에서 에르도안 대통령과의 정상회담 후 공동 언론발표를 통해 “지난해 11월 체결한 ‘원자력 협력 양해각서(MOU)’를 토대로 부지 평가와 공동 워킹그룹 운영 등 튀르키예 시노프 원전 건설 사업을 위한 협력이 순조롭게 진행되고 있다고 평가한다”며 “이러한 성과에서 한 발 더 나아가 ‘원전 프로젝트 금융 협력 MOU’를 체결해 우리 기업의 튀르키예 신규 원전 사업 참여를 선제적으로 지원하기로 했다”고 말했다. 이어 방산 협력에 대해서도 “‘알타이 전차 사업’의 성과를 바탕으로 새로운 방산 협력 분야를 적극 발굴하기로 했다”며 “공동 생산과 기술 협력을...

items.title: 北, 이틀새 또 ‘폭탄비’… 이번엔 순항미사일에 장착
items.snippet: 북한이 2일 순항미사일에 집속탄두를 장착해 위력평가 시험을 했다. 지난달 31일 전술탄도미사일에 이어 탐지·추적이 힘든 순항미사일에도 집속탄두를 실어 대남 초토화 위협을 가한 것. 한 발의 탄두부에서 수백 개의 자탄이 쏟아져 넓은 면적을 파괴하는 집속탄두는 ‘폭탄비’ ‘악마의 무기’로 불린다.북한 조선중앙통신은 전략순항미사일의 중형 산포전투부(집속탄두) 위력평가와 수직타격 비행특성 시험을 2일 진행했다고 3일 보도했다. 북한은 순항미사일의 탄두부에서 쏟아진 집속탄이 해상에 흩뿌려지고, 한국군의 포병진지·탄약고를 상정한 표적을 수직으로 타격하는 사진을 공개했다. 북한은 “순항미사일에 장착된 중형 산포전투부로 5∼6정보(5∼6ha·축구장 7, 8개 면적에 해당)의 표적구역을 초강력 밀도로 초토화할 수 있다는 것을 확증했다”고 주장했다. 발사 후...

items.title: 충남 방산벤처 79곳… 6년 새 매출 38%↑
items.snippet: 충남도 남부출장소는 충남국방벤처센터 협약기업의 매출과 고용이 협약 이후 6년간 각각 37.9%, 9.6% 늘어난 것으로 분석됐다고 3일 밝혔다. 충남국방벤처센터는 방위산업 진입을 희망하는 도내 중소·벤처기업에 기술·경영을 밀착 지원하기 위해 2019년 9월 논산 건양대에 문을 열었다. 현재 도와 논산시, 국방기술진흥연구소가 함께 운영하고 있다. 2019년부터 지난해까지 센터와 협약한 79개 사의 경영 실적을 분석한 결과 매출액은 협약 당시 총 7703억 원에서 지난해 말 1조625억 원으로 2922억 원(37.9%) 늘어났다. 같은 기간 직원 수는 2412명에서 2643명으로 231명(9.6%) 증가했다. 성장은 일부 기업에 그치지 않았다. 79개 사 가운데 73개 사(92%)의 매출이 늘었다. 협약기업은 국비 연구개발(R&D) 과제 확보에서...

items.title: “응급실 압수수색, 의심 정황 있는 경우 등 제한”
items.snippet: 아주대병원 소아전문응급의료센터 압수수색에 대한 의료계 반발이 커지자 정부가 응급실 등 필수의료 분야 압수수색을 최소화하기로 했다. 필수의료 분야에서 사망사고 관련 112 신고가 접수되면 현장 출입 전 병원 관리자와 사전 협의를 하고, 수사는 가급적 비진료 공간에서 진행한다. 정은경 보건복지부 장관은 3일 김종철 경찰청장 직무대행과 만나 이런 내용이 포함된 ‘응급실 등 필수의료 분야 수사 가이드라인’을 논의했다. 압수수색은 형사소송법에 따라 의심할 만한 정황이 있는 경우 등에 한해 제한적으로 실시하기로 했다. 진료를 방해하지 않도록 행정·전산 담당자들과 우선 협의해 최소한의 범위에서 영장을 집행할 방침이다. 경찰 수사가 의료진과 환자 생명에 미치는 영향을 최소화한다는 취지다. 정부는 의료계와 현장 수사관의 의견을 수렴해 구체적인 가이드라인을 마...

items.title: “시간 가는 줄 몰랐어요”… lose와 time 사이에 쓸 말은?
items.snippet: 영국 런던의 대영박물관에서 자유 관람 시간을 즐기고 있습니다. 책에서만 보던 세계적 유물이 바로 눈앞에 있으니 발길이 떨어지지 않습니다. 이 유물 앞에서 한참, 저 조각상 앞에서 또 한참, 정신없이 빠져들다 문득 시계를 보니 가이드와 만나기로 한 시간에서 이미 10분이 훌쩍 지나 있습니다. 화들짝 놀라 약속 장소로 헐레벌떡 뛰어가니, 현지 가이드와 일행이 걱정스러운 표정으로 기다리고 있습니다. 그래서 급히 영어로 “길을 잃은 게 아니라 넋을 잃고 관람하다가 시간 가는 줄 몰랐어요”라고 사과하고 싶은데, 미안한 마음에 당황하기까지 해서 “forget‘과 ’time’이라는 단어만 입안에서 맴돕니다.

items.snippet: 3일 낮 12시쯤 서울 용산구 이태원의 한 샌드위치 가게에서 오토바이 헬멧을 쓴 20대 청년이 나왔다. 짙은 갈색 피부를 가진 이 청년은 손에 든 음식 봉투를 배달용 트렁크에 넣고 오토바이에 올라탔다. 본지 기자가 “한국 분이시냐”고 묻자 그는 “쏘리, 쏘리”라고 답한 뒤 오토바이를 몰고 골목으로 사라졌다. 근처에서 배달하던 이환(26)씨는 “이태원 일대나 신촌 등 서울 번화가에서는 외국인 라이더들을 자주 볼 수 있다”고 했다.

items.title: [알립니다] ‘조선 백일장’ 부울경 예선 조기 마감… 신청 서두르세요
items.snippet: 조선일보사·조선일보미디어연구소·한글학회가 주최하고 교육부가 후원하는 ‘필전 2026-조선 백일장’의 부산·울산·경남(부·울·경) 예선 신청이 조기 마감됐습니다. 당초 4일까지 신청받을 예정이었지만, 신청자가 몰리면서 일찍 마감했습니다. 부·울·경 예선은 7일 부산대에서 열립니다.

items.title: [오늘의 날씨] 2026년 11월 4일
판사들, 與에 부글부글 “전국법관 임시회의 열자”
items.snippet: 조희대 대법원장에 대한 여권의 국회 국정조사 추진과 사퇴 압박 등과 관련해 법원 내부에서 반발이 커지고 있다. 이런 상황에서 3일 전국법관대표회의를 열자는 요구가 나왔다. 남준우 서울회생법원 부장판사는 이날 법원 내부 게시판(코트넷)에 글을 올려 “전례 없는, 그리고 향후 정권과 관계없이 반복될 가능성이 농후한 대법관 재제청 사태와 관련해 전국법관대표회의 임시회의 개최를 촉구한다”고 했다.

items.title: 초대 공소청 수장에 이정현·박철우·예세민 거론
items.snippet: 법무부는 10일이나 11일 검찰총장후보추천위원회(위원장 문무일) 회의를 열고 이재명 정부의 첫 검찰총장 후보군을 추릴 것으로 3일 알려졌다. 검찰총장 후보로는 이정현(58·사법연수원 27기) 검찰총장 직무대행과 박철우(55·30기) 서울중앙지방공소청장이 유력하게 거론된다. 법조계에서는 “이재명 대통령이 기소된 사건의 ‘공소취소’ 문제에 대한 입장이 인선의 변수가 될 것”이란 관측이 나온다.

items.title: 이화영 ‘불법 대북송금’ 재심 신청
items.snippet: 쌍방울 불법 대북 송금 혐의로 기소돼 징역 7년 8개월이 확정돼 복역 중인 이화영 전 경기도 평화부지사가 3일 수원고법에 재심을 청구했다. 이 전 부지사는 대법원에서 유죄가 확정된 혐의 중 외국환거래법 위반 부분과 관련해 무죄를 인정할 증거가 발견됐다고 주장했다.

items.title: 한글 점자의 날 100주년… 손끝으로 세상을 읽다
items.snippet: ‘한글 점자의 날’을 하루 앞둔 3일 경기 수원시 팔달구 경기도시각장애인도서관에서 관계자가 점자책을 읽고 있다. 한글 점자의 날은 1926년 11월 4일 송암 박두성 선생이 한글 점자를 만들어 반포한 것을 기념하는 날이다. 올해 100주년을 맞았다.

items.title: 정부기관 이전 잇단 반발… 과천 시민들 “도시 정체성 해쳐” 시위
items.snippet: 3일 서울 종로구 정부서울청사 앞. 경기 과천 시민 250여 명이 ‘과천을 무시하는 이전 계획, 시민은 거부한다’고 쓴 손팻말을 들고 거리 행진을 벌였다. 같은 시각 청사 안에서는 행정안전부가 ‘2차 중앙행정기관 세종 이전 공청회’를 열었다.

items.title: 점점 심해지는 여학생 학폭… 소년원 가는 소녀, 4년새 2배로
items.snippet: 지난 2월 대전에 사는 A(19)양은 폭행 혐의로 소년원 6개월 송치 처분(소년보호처분 9호)을 받았다. 고등학교를 자퇴하고 ‘학교 밖 청소년’이 된 A양은 또래와 몰려다니며 금품 갈취와 폭행을 반복하다가 피해 학생 신고로 경찰에 적발됐다. 서울의 한 고교에 다니던 B(18)양은 지난 5월 중학교 동창에게 소셜미디어 메시지로 돈을 빌려달라고 요구했다가 거절당하자, 그때부터 계속 협박하고 욕설을 보냈다. B양도 결국 소년부 재판에 넘겨져 사회봉사 명령 처분(3호)을 받았다.

items.title: 중국·홍콩 대학이 ‘톱5’ 싹쓸이… 한국은 올해도 10위 내 못들어
items.snippet: 올해 ‘QS 아시아 대학 평가’에서 ‘톱 5’는 홍콩과 중국 대학이 모두 휩쓸었다. 한국 대학은 6곳이 아시아 상위 20위 안에 들었지만, 2년 연속 10위 안에 포함되지 못했다. 한국 대학의 절반 이상은 작년보다 순위가 떨어졌고, 이 추세는 수도권보다 지방 대학들에서 더 심하게 나타났다.

items.title: 겨울코트 꺼낼까 말까… “오락가락 날씨, 건조한 땅이 원인”
items.snippet: 올가을 들어 사흘 중 하루(35.5%)꼴로 전날 대비 기온 차가 5도 이상인 ‘널뛰기’ 현상을 보인 것으로 나타났다.

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [숨어있는 세계사] 2m 거대 활로… 수적 우세 佛귀족 무찌른 英평민 군대
items.snippet: 얼마 전 미 국방부는 인공지능(AI), 드론, 로봇 등 최첨단 무인 전투 체계의 실전 배치를 획기적으로 당기기 위한 국방 혁신 프로젝트를 발표했어요. 이름은 ‘프로젝트 아쟁쿠르’입니다. ‘아쟁쿠르’는 프랑스의 한 마을 이름인데요. ‘프로젝트 아쟁쿠르’는 중세 백년전쟁 중 있었던 ‘아쟁쿠르 전투’에서 따온 것이에요. 당시 영국군은 장궁(거대한 목재 활)이라는 신기술을 활용해 수적으로 우세하고 단단한 갑옷을 입은 프랑스의 정예 기병을 물리쳤어요. 아쟁쿠르 전투처럼 미 국방부는 신기술(드론·AI·로봇)을 통해 기존의 무겁고 비싼 무기체계를 압도하는 21세기 국방 혁신을 꾀하고 있어요. 오늘은 아쟁쿠르 전투에 대해 알아보도록 할게요.

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [동물 이야기] 나무 잘 타고 물고기 사냥까지… 주택가에서도 사는 ‘전천후 코브라’래요
items.snippet: 얼마 전 아찔한 소식이 들려왔어요. 한 중학생이 자신이 기르는 뱀을 다른 사람에게 팔려고 사육통에서 꺼내다 물리는 바람에 긴급하게 병원으로 실려 가 해독 치료를 받았대요. 이 뱀은 아프리카가 원산지인 숲코브라로 일반인은 허가 없이 거래할 수 없는 종류였어요. 제때 치료받지 않았으면 정말 큰일 날 뻔했죠. 코브라는 아프리카·인도·동남아시아 등 더운 지방을 중심으로 30여 종이 있는데요. 숲코브라는 아프리카에 사는 코브라 중에서 가장 덩치가 커서 다 자란 몸길이는 최장 3m에 육박해요. 이름처럼 원래는 중부 아프리카 지역의 열대 우림에서 살았는데 점차 서식지를 넓혀갔어요.

items.title: ​[신문은 선생님] [예쁜 말 바른 말] [469] ‘안되다’와 ‘안 되다’
items.snippet: “공부가 잘 안돼” “그래도 공부를 포기하면 안 돼” 이 두 문장에는 ‘안돼’라는 표현이 쓰였습니다. 그런데 첫 번째 문장에서는 붙여 쓰고, 두 번째 문장에서는 띄어 썼지요. 그 이유는 무엇일까요?

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [알립니다] ‘어린이조선일보 글로벌 미술 대회’ 접수 연장
items.snippet: 어린이조선일보와 에듀조선이 주최하는 ‘2026년 어린이조선일보 글로벌 미술 대회 & 루브르 박물관 전시회’의 접수 기간이 많은 관심과 요청에 힘입어 23일까지로 연장됐습니다. 입상작은 프랑스 루브르 박물관에 전시되는 기회가 주어집니다. 대상과 금상은 무료 전시 혜택이, 은상부터 장려상까지는 유료 전시 기회가 제공됩니다. ▶참가 대상 : 국내외 영유아, 초등부 / 중·고등, 성인부

items.title: ‘그대 그리고 나’ 소리새 김광석 별세
items.snippet: ‘그대 그리고 나’ ‘아직도 못다한 사랑’ 등으로 1980년대 큰 인기를 끈 포크 그룹 소리새의 멤버 김광석(70)이 3일 오전 별세했다. 1981년 트리오 ‘솔개’를 결성해 트로트를 가미한 ‘아직도 못 다한 사랑’, 블루스 포크 록 ‘연극 중에서’ 등 다양한 장르를 선보였다. 1987년 ‘소리새’로 팀명을 바꾼 뒤 노래 ‘그대 그리고 나’가 큰 성공을 거뒀다. 고인의 마지막 음반 활동은 2015년 소리새의 새 멤버 윤기환과 낸 광복 70주년 기념 듀엣 음반 ‘평화의 강’(북녘땅에 보내는 노래)이다. 빈소는 교원예움 인천사랑병원, 발인은 4일 오후 1시. (032)-441-0404.

items.title: 아동문학계 원로 권오삼 시인 별세
items.snippet: 동시 작가로 한국 아동문학계 원로인 권오삼(83) 시인이 지난달 29일 별세했다. 경북 안동에서 태어난 권 시인은 1975년 ‘월간문학’ 신인상과 ‘소년중앙’ 문학상을 받으며 작품 활동을 시작했다. 주요 동시집으로 ‘진짜랑 깨’ ‘도토리나무가 부르는 슬픈 노래’ ‘개도 잔소리한다’ ‘너도나도 엄지척’ 등이 있다. 그의 작품 ‘발’은 초등학교 국어 교과서에 실렸다.

items.title: ‘편견 없는 가족 보도’ 우수 언론… 가정진흥원, 本紙 등 4곳 선정
items.snippet: 성평등가족부 산하 한국건강가정진흥원이 가족 형태에 대한 차별·편견이 담긴 기사를 쓰지 않은 우수 언론사로 조선일보·한겨레신문·머니투데이·헤럴드경제 등 4곳을 선정했다고 3일 밝혔다. 한국건강가정진흥원은 지난해 6월부터 올해 5월까지 1년간 전국 일간지 25곳의 사회·문화면에 실린 기사를 분석했다. 해당 기사들을 ‘결혼·출산·혈연 중심 가족을 당연시하는가’ ‘가족 내 역할을 성별 고정관념에 기반해 표현하는가’ ‘특정 국가나 민족, 인종, 종교를 차별하거나 비하하는가’ 등의 지표를 기준으로 평가했다. 그 결과 조선일보를 비롯한 4개 매체에서는 차별이나 편견이 담긴 사례가 한 건도 나오지 않았다. 진흥원은 18일 성과 보고회를 열고 이 매체들에 공로패를 줄 예정이다.

items.title: Optical Ceiling on Polaron Mobility in Disordered Molecular Semiconductors: Lessons from Eumelanin
items.abstract: Polaron hopping in disordered molecular semiconductors such as eumelanin is set by energetic disorder $σ$ and reorganization energy $λ$. We show that the reduced polaron absorption band encodes this transport problem. Its value at zero energy fixes the mean hop rate, which bounds the mobility in any dimension. For Gaussian disorder and classical vibrations its centroid is $E_\mathrm{op}=λ+(1-c)σ^2/k_BT$, its variance obeys the Hush relation, and the bound is the Marcus rate at $λ\to E_\mathrm{op}$; a 1D lower bound vanishes at $k_BT^*=(1-c)σ^2/λ$, read from optics.

items.title: Generalized Lorentz Framework for Active Semiconductor Quantum Surface Plasmonics
items.abstract: Nanostructured semiconductors provide an actively tunable platform for light-matter interactions across a broad spectral range. As feature sizes shrink to the deep nanoscale (~10 nm scale), nonclassical carrier dynamics and surface plasmonic responses become prominent, creating substantial challenges for a rigorous and efficient theoretical treatment. Here we develop a generalized Lorentz framework for quantum surface plasmonics in nanostructured semiconductors with arbitrary energymomentum dispersion relations. The framework enables efficient quantitative treatment of carrier nonlocality, carrier surface accumulation and depletion, and nonlocal damping in three-dimensional semiconductor nanostructures, under electrical tuning and across a wide range of doping densities. items.title: A RISC-V Simulator for the Tenstorrent Tensix Architecture
items.abstract: RISC-V based AI accelerators have become popular and not only for AI and ML, but also as vehicles for exploring HPC workloads more generally. Tenstorrent are one example, and whilst they document their Tensix architecture in detail and develop their software stack openly, running code has historically required a physical card, and their recently released simulator targets hardware equivalence rather than introspection. In this paper we present Wolfpine, a community developed RISC-V simulator for the Tensix architecture, supporting both the Wormhole and Blackhole generations and integrating seamlessly with the TT-Metal software stack. Constructed entirely from publicly available documentation, open source software and measurements on physical hardware, Wolfpine is written in pure Python for readability and ease of modification. An opt-in, provenance-tracked cost model adds timing fidelity...

items.title: Effect of compensation on magnetic ordering in (Ga,Mn)As
items.abstract: The real mechanism of ferromagnetism in III-V diluted magnetic semiconductors such as Ga$_{1-x}$Mn$_x$As is still debated. The experimental results point out the realization of appreciable ferromagnetism at filling of the impurity band close to one-half that can be expressed in terms of compensation degree. Based on our recent results on the existence of two competing mechanisms of pair indirect exchange (with ferro- and antiferro alignment of Mn $d$ shells), a theory of magnetic ordering in (Ga,Mn)As is presented. The molecular-field-like equation is derived in which the effective exchange constant contains all necessary information about material, including the Mn content, the compensation degree, the crystal coordination, and the parameters of two competing pair exchange interactions. Wavefront engineering with atomic Huygens' surfaces made simple
items.abstract: Atomic arrays provide a cooperative platform for light-mediated interactions in nonlocal metasurfaces which can operate in the quantum regime without nanofabricated optical elements or intrinsic material absorption. We present a minimal atomic implementation to harness wavefront engineering and create a near-ideal intrinsic atomic Huygens' surface. A simple bilayer square lattice with a two-atom unit cell, not limited to small lattice spacings, provides near-unity reflectionless transmission and a full $2π$ phase control of transmitted light without the localized site-dependent level shifts of previous proposals. This simplification is achieved through nonlocal radiative excitations that provide the familiar electric-dipole response with even radiation parity as well as an odd-parity radiation channel whose leading multipolar interpretation combines magnetic-dipole and electric-quadrupol...

items.title: Analytically Calibrated Upper L-Statistics for High-Dimensional Mean Change-Point Testing
items.abstract: This paper develops upper L-statistic methods for testing and localizing a high-dimensional mean change. At each candidate split, the proposed statistics rank the squared studentized CUSUM values across coordinates and aggregate either a fixed number or a fixed proportion of the largest entries. This construction connects max-type and sum-type procedures and provides sensitivity to a wide range of sparsity regimes. We establish asymptotic null distributions under an independent-component representation allowing weak cross-sectional dependence. The limiting laws are Poisson tangent processes for fixed ranks and Gaussian-process or Gumbel laws for proportional ranks. To improve finite-sample performance, we develop analytic calibrations for marginal variance estimation, cross-sectional dependence, extreme clustering, and skewness, and establish their first-order validity. items.title: Bezier-GP: Bezier-Surface-Based Gaussian Process for Chips-on-Wafer Warpage Modeling
items.abstract: As the semiconductor industry transitions to the post-Moore paradigm, wafer warpage has become a critical quality issue in advanced packaging; particularly for 3D stacking and high-bandwidth memory manufacturing where die-level deformation can affect bonding quality, interconnect reliability, and yield. However, direct high-throughput measurement of individual chip warpage remains difficult in mass-production environments, while existing wafer-level metrology systems routinely provide dense 3D shape data at the wafer scale. This paper proposes a Bezier-surface-based Gaussian Process---known as Bezier-GP---for chips-on-wafer warpage modeling. items.title: Temperature-Independent Logarithmic Current Slope in Interdiffusion-Broadened Silicon pn Junction toward Low-Power Thermometry
items.abstract: With the development of cryogenic technologies such as quantum computing, there is an increasing need for low-power cryogenic thermometers that minimize self-heating. Here, we report an anomalous temperature-independent logarithmic current slope, $d(\ln J)/dV$, in heavily doped silicon p$^{+}$n$^{+}$ junctions with significant dopant interdiffusion and highlight the advantages of our device as a low-power, cryogenic thermometer. Electrical characterizations from 2 to 420 K reveal that, at low forward bias, $d(\ln J)/dV$ remains nearly constant, which yields a voltage-temperature responsivity that is nearly independent of bias current. The observed transport cannot be fully understood with conventional diffusion or direct band-to-band tunneling. Instead, the results suggest the contribution of trap-assisted tunneling. These results establish interdiffusion-broadened silicon p$^{+}$n$^{+}$...

items.title: Polariton tweezers
items.abstract: The non-invasive, deterministic manipulation of charge carriers remains a fundamental challenge in solid-state quantum technologies. Here, we demonstrate the concept of dynamic polariton tweezers capable of trapping and transporting electrons across a two-dimensional electron system via the long-range electrostatic potential of dipolar (d-) exciton-polaritons. By driving a semiconductor microcavity with a specifically engineered, non-collinear three-beam optical pump with TE-polarization, we synthesize a macroscopic polariton lattice with hexagonal symmetry. The spatially periodic field of this d-polariton condensate acts as a reconfigurable trapping landscape for the electrons. items.title: Cage-enforced i-wave altermagnetism in boron-carbon clathrates
items.abstract: The spin splitting of an altermagnet arises from a rotation that relates its two magnetic sublattices. In known cases it is fixed by the crystal structure. Here we show that guest-host frameworks separate the two roles. In the boron-carbon clathrates $M$B$_3$C$_3$ the ordered cage removes the translation between the two guest sites and enforces cubic $i$-wave altermagnetism, with six symmetry-enforced nodal planes, for any magnetic guest in the compensated state; strain retunes the class to $d$- or $g$-wave. We demonstrate the platform with GdB$_3$C$_3$: its compensated antiferromagnetic ground state is a narrow-gap semiconductor with spin splitting of 0.19 eV at the conduction-band edge, and its weakly pinned Néel vector switches the helicity-resolved optical response on and off according to the magnetic point group. items.abstract: Lattice-mismatched heteroepitaxy is limited by misfit dislocations, threading defects, and residual strain generated at buried interfaces. Here, we show that current-confined electrochemistry transforms the Ge/Si heterointerface into a laterally continuous nanometric free surface while preserving the Ge epilayer. A low-doped Ge layer on a conductive p-type Si substrate redirects anodization current toward the misfit-dislocation-rich interface. Numerical modelling including charge-transfer kinetics shows that this confinement arises from hole-limited charge transfer and, together with electrochemical calibration, defines a process window that combines interfacial current confinement with controlled Si porosification. items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VII. Step kinetics
items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the kinetics of attachment of new segments of the crystalline lattice (pyramids) at steps on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs(-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb(-1-1-1) surfaces. Diffusion species are gallium adatoms at high coverage or gallium adatoms connected with nonmetal atom creating stable pyramids. These pyramids arrive at the steps, and cannot be attached be directly because the Ga adatom at the pyramid base cannot be attached directly. Therefore they are incorporated into the step by additional nonmetal atoms glue atoms arriving from the vapor or detached from other segments of the surface terraces.

items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VI. Surface diffusion on a nonmetal-terminated surface
items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate surface diffusion of adsorbates on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs (-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb (-1-1-1) surfaces. The mixed coverage consists of Ga adatoms in the first layer with a nonmetal atom attached above them forming a triangular-based pyramid. The pyramidal structures are stable during surface jumps involving rotations around one of the basal Ga adatoms. Thus, the diffusion proceeds via rotation (pivot) of the pair of the other basal Ga adatoms around an immobile Ga adatom moving them into new, originally empty sites. items.title: Gate-tunable superconductor-semiconductor coupling and its impact on zero-energy modes in PbTe-Pb nanowires
items.abstract: Superconductor-semiconductor coupling in hybrid nanowires plays a pivotal role in Majorana devices. Here, we demonstrate this tunable coupling in PbTe-Pb nanowires and its impact on the induced gap and zero-bias peaks (ZBPs). In the strong coupling regime, the device reveals a clean superconducting gap, where robust and non-robust ZBPs are observed in distinct magnetic field ranges. Conversely, increasing the gate voltage drives the system toward the weak coupling regime, where the gap becomes narrow and soft. Consequently, robust ZBPs disappear while non-robust ones persist. Our results establish a direct link between tunable coupling and robust ZBPs, providing guidelines on engineering Majorana zero modes and topological qubits.

items.title: Amplification of valley polarization in an hBN-separated MoSe2-WSe2 heterostructure
items.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenide heterostructures host long-lived interlayer excitons in the +K and -K valleys that can encode long-lived valley polarization. We investigated the low-temperature valley polarization dynamics in an MoSe2-bilayer hBN-WSe2 heterostructure. The bilayer hBN spacer results in an interlayer exciton lifetime exceeding 2 μs and an anomalous valley polarization amplification effect. Our theoretical model shows that this amplification results from the long exciton lifetime and exciton-exciton interactions. This work sets the stage for long-lived interlayer excitons to be used in nonlinear valleytronic transistors and amplifiers.

items.title: Optical Detection of Coefficient of Thermal Expansion via Frequency Tracking at Cryogenic Temperatures
items.abstract: Accurate characterization of the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) in nanoscale thin films is critical for predicting residual stress and ensuring the reliability of modern micro-electromechanical systems and advanced semiconductor architectures. The primary limitation is that traditional methods depend on precise thickness measurements or are restricted to crystalline materials. In this work, we present an in-situ, non-destructive optical methodology to determine the CTE of suspended nanofilms by tracking the temperature-dependence of their vibrational frequency. This approach eliminates thickness measurements entirely and works for amorphous films where X-ray diffraction (XRD) fails. items.title: Band Alignment of Grafted versus Directly Bonded Si/Ge Heterostructures
items.abstract: The electronic properties of semiconductor heterostructures are influenced by the local bonding and electrostatic environment at the heterointerface. Here, we investigate how the interface-formation mechanism modifies the band alignment of Si/Ge heterostructures by directly comparing Al2O3-mediated semiconductor grafting with direct bonding. Interface-sensitive X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy combined with Kraut analysis reveals type-I band alignment for both structures, but with different band offsets: the valence-band offset increases from ~0.08 eV for directly bonded Si/Ge to ~0.21 eV for grafted Si/Al2O3/Ge, accompanied by a corresponding reduction in the conduction-band offset. Raman spectroscopy further distinguishes the two interfacial configurations. items.title: Nondestructive 3D Metrology of Through-Glass Via Geometry and Internal Wall Texture Using Holotomography
items.abstract: Through-glass vias (TGVs) are increasingly important for semiconductor packaging, yet their internal geometry and wall texture remain difficult to characterize nondestructively. Here, we use holotomography (HT) to inspect the three-dimensional (3D) geometry and internal wall texture of intact, unfilled TGVs before metallization. HT reconstructs the refractive index (RI) distribution of the glass and via. Maps of RI and spatially filtered RI then localize the internal boundary. Geometric fitting quantifies via dimensions and taper, while spatial filtering separates slowly varying wall form from finer texture. The reconstructed surface supports volumetric visualization, dimensional measurements and spatial characterization of wall texture within one optical inspection workflow. items.title: Trapping photo-carriers in undoped gate-defined quantum dots using an on-chip microwave resonator for charge readout
items.abstract: Scaling up gate-defined quantum dot systems is hindered by the rapid growth in the number of control gates. To tackle this challenge, we propose a different approach where the quantum dots are created from optically generated charges trapped beneath accumulation gates. By shining an above-the-gap laser light onto an undoped GaAs substrate, we demonstrate that it is possible to create and separate electron-hole pairs to form quantum dots. For the charge readout, we use a superconducting coplanar waveguide resonator capacitively coupled to the quantum dots. With these elements, we demonstrate a working many-charge double quantum dot device comprised of only two plunger gates, one tunnel coupling gate and one sensing gate. items.title: Cryogenic performance of Silicon Photo-Multipliers at LN$_2$ temperature and at 3 K in the RES-NOVA cryostat
items.abstract: Silicon Photo-Multipliers (SiPMs) are semiconductor-based photodetectors that offer performance comparable to that of traditional Photo-Multiplier Tubes (PMTs), while providing several advantages, including low operating voltage, immunity to magnetic fields, compact size, and mechanical robustness. These features have led to their widespread adoption in scintillator-based detectors for both fundamental and applied physics. In recent years, there has been a growing interest in the detection of scintillation light at cryogenic temperatures in low-temperature experiments based on bolometric detectors, such as RES-NOVA and CUPID, as well as in emerging quantum applications. In the RES-NOVA experiment, radiopure PbWO$_4$ crystals are used to detect supernova neutrinos. items.title: Self-driven beta-radiation detection through a graphene/water/silicon heterostructure
items.abstract: Large-volume neutrino observatories, exemplified by IceCube, exploit Cherenkov light generated by neutrino-induced charged particles in Antarctic ice, highlighting the potential of water-based media for high-energy particle detection. In $β$-decay, a neutron converts into a proton via the weak interaction, emitting an electron and an electron antineutrino. The electron constitutes the beta radiation detected in this work, while the accompanying antineutrino motivates future extensions toward neutrino detection. items.title: Energy Transfer and Strong Coupling in Plasmonic Systems
items.abstract: The coupling between plasmon resonances of metal nanostructures and electronic excitations of molecular/semiconductor systems is important in a number of applications, including surface enhanced spectroscopy, hot-electron catalysis, plasmon-induced resonance energy transfer and the creation of hybrid light-matter states. The past several decades has seen a large number of experimental studies of these effects, as well as the development of theory to explain the results. In this Perspectives article we use classical electromagnetic (EM) simulations to examine how the localized surface plasmon resonances (LSPRs) of metal nanoparticles and propagating surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) in extended metal nanostructures (wires/plates/films) are affected by interactions with a molecular/semiconductor system. items.title: Cross-Scale Spatial Reasoning: A Learning-Centered Framework for Designing Immersive Learning Environments
items.abstract: Understanding complex scientific and engineering systems often requires learners to connect structures, processes, and behaviors across different spatial scales and levels of organization. Although research on spatial cognition, scale, multiple representations, and systems thinking has examined aspects of this challenge, these perspectives do not always provide explicit guidance for designing learning activities that require learners to integrate information across levels. Immersive technologies offer opportunities to explore otherwise inaccessible structures, coordinate representations, and investigate system behavior, but their educational value depends on the reasoning they support. items.title: Reasoning Across Scales: Learning Challenges and Opportunities for Immersive Technologies in Chip Design Education
items.abstract: As demand for semiconductor talent grows, education must prepare learners for the complexity of modern chip design. Instruction typically relies on lectures, textbooks, software exercises, and limited laboratory experiences. Although foundational, these approaches offer limited support for understanding the spatial, multi-scale, and interconnected nature of chip design. Virtual reality (VR) can help learners visualize and interact with complex structures and processes, but its educational opportunities remain underexplored. We examined this gap through chip design curriculum analysis and semi-structured interviews with five participants representing instructional and learner perspectives. We characterized four learning demands: descriptive knowledge, procedural knowledge, relational and design-focused reasoning, and strategic decision-making. We identified challenges in connecting abstra...

items.title: Visualizing Anisotropic Charge Transport in CrSBr using Bias-Dependent Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
items.abstract: Anisotropic semiconductors offer unique opportunities for next-generation electronics due to their direction-dependent transport. However, conventional electrical measurements provide only spatially averaged characteristics. Here, we employ bias-dependent Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) to directly visualize the response of CrSBr under different electrical bias configurations. Spatially resolved KPFM maps reveal highly distinct, crystallographic-direction-dependent potential profiles. To elucidate this behavior, we employ anisotropic transport simulations that capture the charge transport and electric-field distributions in CrSBr. The close agreement between experiment and simulation provides a unified picture of anisotropic charge transport and bias-induced potential redistribution. items.abstract: Virtual metrology (VM) aims to estimate costly or delayed metrology variables from heterogeneous sensor signals and in-line measurements, and it acts as a critical component of semiconductor manufacturing. While recent data-driven models have improved VM accuracy, most are trained in batch settings and assume stationary data distributions. In practice, however, production environments evolve continuously due to equipment degradation, process adjustments, and maintenance events, making conventional batch-trained VM models difficult to maintain under temporal distribution shifts. In this work, we propose GRAPE (Global Regression with Adaptive Prediction Enhancement), a practical online learning framework for VM in evolving wafer-processing environments. items.title: A Mixed-Precision CNN-LSTM Accelerator Featuring Long-Kernel Memory Reuse and Dynamic Quantization for Sleep Staging
items.abstract: This letter presents a mixed-precision CNN-LSTM accelerator for EEG-based sleep staging. To efficiently execute long temporal convolutions, a serpentine dataflow propagates activations between neighboring processing elements, reducing memory accesses by 6.2 times and 2.25 times compared with output- and weight-stationary dataflows, respectively. A hybrid quantization scheme applies runtime dynamic quantization to the LSTM and MLP layers and assigns mixed precision on a layer-by-layer basis, reducing model size by 4.16 times. Combined with a bit-flexible MAC architecture and channel-grouped memory scheduling, the accelerator supports INT2/4/8/16 inference. Fabricated in 65 nm CMOS, the accelerator consumes 0.40 mW and achieves a 258 times speedup over an iso-frequency 32b RISC-V processor. items.title: Effect of Rapid Thermal Annealing on the Superconductivity of ALD-Grown TiN thin films
items.abstract: Titanium nitride (TiN) is a promising superconducting material for scalable quantum technologies owing to its tunable kinetic inductance and compatibility with CMOS thin-film processing. However, the superconducting performance of atomic-layer-deposited TiN can be degraded by oxygen incorporation, off-stoichiometry, and crystallographic disorder. In this work, we investigate rapid thermal annealing (RTA) in high-purity nitrogen as a post-deposition strategy to improve polycrystalline TiN films grown by RF-biased plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition. Grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction reveals reduced peak broadening, a smaller lattice parameter, and a stronger (111) preferred orientation with increasing annealing temperature. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy depth profiling shows reduced oxygen-related bonding and a shift toward a Ti--N-dominated chemical environment after annealing....

items.abstract: This paper proposes an open-source automated LC matching network optimization framework that combines schematic-level design optimization with electromagnetic (EM)-aware post-layout refinement. An ML-based surrogate predicts the frequency-dependent complex admittance of individual routes, enabling reuse across matching network topologies and physical layouts for the same technology node without retraining. Low Frequency Noise Identification for the SuperCDMS Experiment using Convolutional Neural Networks
items.abstract: The SuperCDMS experiment uses semiconductor crystal detectors operated at cryogenic temperatures to search for low-mass dark matter. Vibrations observed during the SuperCDMS Soudan experiment generated broadband low-frequency noise (LFN), which due to its similarity in the pulse shape to the low-energy signal events is difficult to remove. In the final low ionization threshold analysis, CDMSlite Run 3, the strong event selection criterion applied to remove LFN events also significantly reduced the ability to identify signal events in the low energy region, thus reducing the sensitivity of the experiment to low-mass dark matter. Therefore, an LFN rejection criterion using machine learning (ML) aimed to improve the signal efficiency while maintaining the signal purity has now been developed. This paper presents a new method using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), its application to the...

items.title: Field-resolved observation and quantification of the instantaneous Kerr response in semiconductors
items.abstract: The optical Kerr effect, whereby the refractive index of a material changes with light intensity, underpins nonlinear photonics and emerging mid-infrared technologies. Accurate determination of the nonlinear refractive index is therefore essential, yet conventional intensity-based techniques infer the nonlinear phase shift indirectly from changes in beam propagation or optical spectra. Moreover, methods such as the $z$-scan cannot resolve the temporal evolution of the nonlinear response, making it difficult to distinguish instantaneous Kerr nonlinearities from delayed contributions, including free-carrier effects. Here, we investigate the nonlinear optical response of germanium at $5 μ\mathrm{m}$ using field-resolved degenerate pump-probe spectroscopy. By measuring the transmitted probe electric field as a function of pump-probe delay, we directly retrieve the pump-induced phase shift an...

items.title: Full-Potential Korringa Kohn Rostoker Study of Structural and Mechanical Properties in SiGeSn Alloys
items.abstract: Accurate first-principles descriptions of open, covalently bonded crystal structures remain challenging within conventional Korringa--Kohn--Rostoker (KKR) approaches owing to the spherical approximations commonly employed for the effective crystal potential. Here, we systematically assess the recently developed full-potential KKR (KKR-FP) implementation in the open-source MuST package and demonstrate its applicability to diamond-structured group-IV semiconductors and SiGeSn alloys. Benchmark calculations for diamond-structured Si reveal substantial limitations of the conventional muffin-tin and atomic sphere approximations, whereas KKR-FP accurately reproduces the experimental equilibrium lattice parameter and bulk modulus, yielding 5.433 and 94.9 GPa. The full-potential treatment also recovers the semiconducting character of Si. Further calculations for elemental Ge and Sn establish the...

items.title: Dipolar Exciton Polarons in a van der Waals Homobilayer
items.abstract: Fermi polarons exemplify how many-body interactions give rise to emergent quasiparticles, providing a fundamental framework for understanding interacting quantum matter. In electron-doped two-dimensional semiconductors, exciton polarons offer optical access to Fermi-polaron physics and electrical tunability, yet achieving stronger and more controllable exciton-electron interactions remains a key challenge. Here, we realize dipolar exciton polarons in an electrically tunable van der Waals homobilayer, where interlayer excitons with spatially separated electrons and holes act as quantum impurities carrying permanent electric dipole moments. These dipolar polarons exhibit substantially enhanced exciton-electron interactions, with binding energies more than four times those of conventional intralayer exciton polarons. We further demonstrate that Fermi-sea layer polarization provides an addit...

items.title: Photonic Crystal Integrated Graphene-Silicon Schottky Diodes for Resonant Infrared Photodetection
items.abstract: Narrowband infrared (IR) photodetection has become a critical technology for the next generation of smart low-power photodetectors. In this work, we present a device based on a graphene-silicon Schottky junction with narrowband response in the short-wave IR (SWIR) regime. Integrating a photonic crystal (PhC) slab in the device enables a wavelength dependant tailoring of graphene absorption. The devices were characterized by photocurrent measurement, which was enhanced more than two orders of magnitude by the PhC integration. The sharp enhancements obtained can also be predicted by numerical simulation. This approach offers a highly scalable, tunable, CMOS-compatible architecture for narrowband IR photodetection, paving the way for next-generation, low-power IR sensors.

items.abstract: We present a comprehensive density functional theory (DFT) investigation of the structural, mechanical, electronic, optical, thermoelectric, and bonding properties of Y2CdX4 (X = S, Se, Te) compounds for potential optoelectronic and energy-conversion applications. Structural optimization reveals a systematic expansion of the equilibrium lattice parameters from S to Te. The calculated bulk moduli decrease from 83 GPa for Y2CdS4 to 68 GPa for Y2CdSe4 and 54 GPa for Y2CdTe4, indicating progressive lattice softening. Electronic band-structure calculations predict indirect band gaps of 2.42, 2.08, and 1.71 eV for Y2CdS4, Y2CdSe4, and Y2CdTe4, respectively, with further narrowing upon inclusion of spin-orbit coupling. items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to elucidate the properties of the polar surfaces of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors, i.e., metal- and nonmetal-terminated. The systems considered were clean wurtzite gallium nitride (i.e. (0001) and (000-1) GaN surfaces), zinc blende gallium phosphide (i.e. (111) and (-1-1-1) GaP), gallium arsenide (i.e. (111) and (-1-1-1) GaAs), and (111) and (-1-1-1) GaSb surfaces. The calculated data include the crystallographic structure and the electronic states of the termination atoms on both sides, i.e. their positions, energies, and occupations. All nonmetal-terminated surfaces exhibit no reconstruction, and their broken-bond states are located in the vicinity of the valence band maxima (VBM), pinning the Fermi level. items.title: Quantifying Blinking Suppression and Probing Its Mechanism in PPD-Treated Single Quantum Dots
items.abstract: Colloidal semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) are highly promising materials for various applications, yet photoluminescence intermittency (blinking) remains a key obstacle to their practical use. While recent advances have enabled partial or complete suppression of this effect, both the degree of suppression and the mechanism by which it occurs are often difficult to establish. In the present work we analyse the blinking suppression of single CdSe/ZnS QDs after treatment with p-phenylenediamine (PPD), recently discovered by Yang et al. We revisit the blinking mechanism in this system and show that it is governed predominantly by the trapping mechanism, rather than by Auger ionization as previously proposed. items.abstract: To accelerate materials discovery, language models must be able to address problems at the research frontier. Yet textbook- and examination-derived benchmarks primarily assess established knowledge, leaving performance on frontier research problems largely untested. We introduce FrontierMat, a benchmark of 330 problems drawn from frontier academic and industrial research in fields including aerospace, semiconductors, embodied intelligence and nuclear fusion. Every problem is validated by leading experimentalists and industry experts in its field. Each problem presents a real study and asks the model to infer a withheld outcome or draw a conclusion from selected experimental evidence. Problems are annotated by functional domain, material system and the scale of the governing mechanism; 130 require cross-scale reasoning. items.title: Unifying dynamical electron-electron and electron-phonon interactions from first principles
items.abstract: Electron-phonon interactions in materials with free carriers are dynamically screened by low-energy electronic excitations, yet first-principles calculations almost always treat this screening in the adiabatic approximation. items.abstract: Untrusted third-party entities throughout the semiconductor supply chain expose proprietary hardware intellectual property to reverse engineering, piracy, and overproduction. While logic locking counters this threat by embedding key-dependent logic, conventional static key-gates remain vulnerable to both oracle-guided SAT attacks and structural removal attacks due to their time-invariant netlist signatures. items.title: 10 kV $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ Sub-Bandgap Triggered Impurity Photoconductive Semiconductor Switches (i-PCSSs): Lessons for Optimal Design
items.abstract: $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ photoconductive semiconductor switches (PCSSs) are attractive for high-voltage operation, but above-bandgap triggering requires deep-ultraviolet excitation. Here, we investigate a 650-um-thick, 0.01% Fe-doped $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ impurity PCSS with a 5-mm lateral gap under continuous-wave (CW) 808-nm sub-bandgap excitation at biases up to 10 kV ( 20 kV cm^-1). The device exhibited clear sub-bandgap photoconductive switching. As the optical power density increased from 0.64 to 3.18 W cm^-2, the ON-state current increased progressively while the ON-state resistance decreased, consistent with enhanced defect-assisted photocarrier generation. A higher applied bias further strengthened the switching response through enhanced field-assisted carrier transport. items.title: Complete Au-free Metallization Platform for UWBG Al$_{0.65}$Ga$_{0.35}$N channel MOS-HEMTs using Ti/Al/Ti Ohmic Contacts and Refractory TiN/Pt Gates
items.abstract: Au-free ohmic contacts and refractory gate stacks are critical for integrating ultra-wide-bandgap (UWBG) Al-rich AlGaN transistors with Si-CMOS technology. In this work, we demonstrate, to our knowledge, the first complete Au-free metallization platform for Al$_{0.65}$Ga$_{0.35}$N-channel MOS-HEMTs, combining electron-beam-evaporated and sputtered Ti/Al/Ti ohmic contacts with sputtered TiN and Pt gate metals. The Ti/Al/Ti contacts achieved a contact resistance of approximately 7.5--7.7 $Ω\cdot$mm while being fully Au-free. This contact resistance is achieved using a 600 $^\circ$C anneal, substantially below the 850--950 $^\circ$C typically required for Au-capped Ti/Al/X/Au contacts on Al-rich AlGaN, indicating a reduced thermal budget and improved compatibility with silicon-CMOS foundries. items.title: Efficient Simulation of Gate Leakage Currents in Ultra-scaled Transistors from First Principles
items.abstract: To ensure high electrostatic integrity in ultra-scaled field-effect transistors (FETs), thin gate dielectric layers are typically needed, potentially giving rise to (strong) leakage currents. Being able to model this effect is therefore crucial. Here, we show how gate leakage currents can be computed at the ab initio level in WS$_2$-hBN FETs by extending the well-established quantum transmitting boundary method (QTBM). Two main challenges are tackled: (i) the calculation of the open boundary conditions (OBCs) for the gate contacts and (ii) the solution of the resulting sparse linear system of equations A x = b where the matrix A possesses an unstructured sparsity pattern. We demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the state of the art and can be readily applied to simulate transistors with gate lengths exceeding 25 nm.

items.title: Electric field control of anisotropic spin traffic between spin-filtering and magnon-scattering in a layered antiferromagnet
items.abstract: Layered A-type antiferromagnetic (AFM) semiconductors offer a unique platform for spintronic devices by combining robust magnetism with gate-tunable semiconducting properties. We present a dual-gate field-effect transistor based on CrSBr, a layered A-type AFM with pronounced transport anisotropy and complex spin dynamics. Our device provides independent control over carrier density and displacement field. Systematic transport measurements reveal that the displacement field, rather than doping, predominantly governs the sign and magnitude of magnetoresistance ratio (MRR). We identify the origins of both negative and positive MRR components and connect them to interlayer and intralayer spin-dependent transport mechanisms. items.title: Uncertainty-aware Feedback Loop Diagnosis: integrating reinforcement learning and conformal prediction for reliable wafer defect classification
items.abstract: Semiconductor manufacturing is a complex, multi-step process that requires both high precision and low operating costs. Therefore, detecting defects in a high-volume setting is an important component of wafer map analysis for reliable production. However, most state-of-the-art deep learning approaches require a full scan of the surface, which hinders the development of high-throughput inspection systems. To address this problem, we propose Uncertainty-aware Feedback Loop Diagnosis (UFLD), a novel algorithm that employs reinforcement learning for adaptive measurement acquisition and provides a prediction uncertainty level after each step, stopping the process once sufficient information is obtained. items.title: Cubic-Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te optical modes across the phonon and phonon-polariton regimes
items.abstract: Alloying offers a convenient route to tune the physical properties of semiconductors, at the price, however, of local lattice/bond distortions needed to accommodate the lattice mismatch. Being nearly lattice-matched and moreover highly resistant to lattice and bond distortions thanks to a largely covalent bonding, cubic Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te sets a benchmark to test the sensitivity of lattice vibrations to minimum lattice and bond distortions induced by alloying. We explore experimentally the two transverse optical regimes of cubic Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te (x<0.7), with ab initio calculations in support: (1) the phonon-polariton regime at quasi-infinite (photon-like) wavelengths averaging over the alloy disorder, probed by forward-Raman scattering, and (2) the purely-mechanical phonon regime down to minimum wavelengths nearly matching the lattice constant zooming into the alloy disorder, achieved by inel...

items.title: Electronic liquid crystals and superconductivity from doping a moiré Mott insulator
items.abstract: Electronic liquid crystals, such as stripe phases and nematics, are self-organized states of matter with spontaneously broken rotational symmetry. They are expected to emerge in a doped Mott insulator as a compromise between short- and long-range Coulomb interactions, and are believed to be intimately connected to the emergence of high temperature superconductivity either as a competing order or an intertwined order. Moiré semiconductors provide a controllable platform to explore the relationship between stripe phases and superconductivity near a Mott insulator. Here we report the generic appearance of stripe phases in a doped moiré Mott insulator and the observation of a stripe to-superconductor quantum phase transition in twisted bilayer WSe2. items.title: Confinement Controlled Phase-Pure 2D Layered Perovskites for Band-Edge Engineering
items.abstract: Controlling the number n of connected octahedra layers in two-dimensional metal halide perovskites enables fine control of the semiconductor band gap that is highly advantageous for optoelectronic and light emission applications. Phase purity in terms of n is crucial towards narrow emission bands and the design of band structure alignment for charge carrier funneling. We present a simple and scalable synthesis method using cesium and butylammonium as A-cations to fabricate microcrystal powders of 2D lead bromide perovskites that results in samples with very high n-phase purity. The obtained microcrystals show a sharp onset in absorbance and single narrow emission peak in UV-blue spectral range, and we confirm their structure and composition with X-ray diffraction and energy dispersive spectroscopy. items.title: SKFitter: Symmetry resolved Slater Koster tight-binding models from first principles for s, p, d and f electrons, spin orbit coupling and magnetism
items.abstract: Constructing accurate and physically interpretable tight binding (TB) Hamiltonians from first principles calculations remains challenging, particularly for materials exhibiting complex orbital hybridization, spin orbit coupling (SOC), and magnetic order. SKFitter is an open-source Python framework for constructing and optimizing symmetry resolved Slater Koster TB models directly from density functional theory (DFT) calculations performed using Quantum ESPRESSO or VASP. The framework supports s to f orbitals, incorporates on site SOC and site resolved magnetic exchange interactions, and accommodates both orthogonal and nonorthogonal basis. A central feature is the symmetry resolved parameterization of orbital manifolds, which allows independent two centre hopping integrals between symmetry allowed orbital groups and across distinct neighbour shells. items.title: PDE-based Bayesian Inverse Problems in All-at-once Framework
items.abstract: We propose a modern all-at-once framework for PDE-based Bayesian inversion by introducing the PDE residual as probabilistic information. In this framework, the PDE residual is treated as a soft constraint with a residual covariance and is directly incorporated into the likelihood function. The new hybrid likelihood function eliminates PDE solves, thus reducing expensive computational costs, while performing rigorous Bayesian inference. Theoretically, we establish the well-posedness of the posterior with uncertainty quantification, and numerically, we propose two efficiency inversion algorithms based on two posterior sampling methods. In particular, one algorithm is based on Metropolis-within-Gibbs MCMC method with a PDE-informed block- diagonal Gaussian prior, and the other is based on a joint sampling strategy. items.title: Growth and morphology of core-shell nanowires incorporating dissimilar hexagonal semiconductors: the case of InAs-ZnTe
items.abstract: Core-shell nanowires incorporating semiconductors from two groups, III-V for the core and II-VI for the shell, have been grown by molecular beam epitaxy in two dedicated chambers connected under ultra-high vacuum, and studied by electron microscopy. During the growth of the shell, the wurtzite structure of the core is replicated in the shell, without any creation of defects. This is true for a wide range of shell thickness, from about one monolayer, up to 25 nm thanks to the good lattice match between the InAs material of the core and the ZnTe material of the shell. While (1 100) m-facets and (11 20) a-facets coexist on the sidewalls of the core, during the growth of the ZnTe shell the size of the m-facets progressively increases at the expense of the a-facets which eventually disappear. items.title: I$_4$ complex acting as near-infrared emitter with a quantum memory in silicon
items.abstract: Silicon color centers emitting in the near infrared offer a route to spin--photon interfaces compatible with mature complementary metal--oxide--semiconductor fabrication. A key unresolved candidate is the X-line at 1039.7 meV in the photoluminescence (PL) spectrum, long attributed to a complex of four self-interstitials (I$_4$), yet whose microscopic structure and spin properties have remained controversial and uncharacterized at a predictive level. Using hybrid-functional (HSE06) density functional theory, we unambiguously establish the bare I$_4$ complex as the origin of the X-line: our calculations quantitatively reproduce the zero-phonon line, the complete phonon sideband structure---identifying the prominent secondary peaks as one- and two-phonon replicas of strongly coupled quasi-local modes---and the EPR hyperfine constants. items.title: Implementation and Validation of Mismatch-Tolerant High-Gain OTA with a Calibrated Negative Conductance Load
items.abstract: This paper presents the circuit-level implementation of a mismatch-tolerant high-gain operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) using automatic negative-conductance calibration in 65-nm CMOS. The technique enhances OTA gain by compensating for its finite output conductance using a cross-coupled transistor pair, with an on-chip calibration loop that eliminates the need for a replica circuit or external tuning. The calibration routine increases the gain by driving the steady state error of the OTA in a unity gain feedback loop toward zero. The implementation addresses practical challenges involving comparator offset, DAC design, and subtractor gain and offset. A 6-bit capacitive DAC (CDAC)-based comparator offset calibration scheme enables reliable detection of the sub-millivolt steady state error required for high OTA gain. items.title: OPERA: OPamp Design by an Expert-Taught Reasoning Agent, from Specifications to Layout
items.abstract: Analog flows from specifications to a signed-off layout rarely run without manual iteration. Recent large language model (LLM) agents size circuits with optimizer loops over the device dimensions and stop at the schematic. We present OPERA (OPamp design by an Expert-taught Reasoning Agent), in which a general-purpose LLM agent designs CMOS opamps from specifications to post-layout sign-off with open-source tools. First, the designer teaches the agent the gm/ID method: map the specifications to transconductances and minimum currents, choose gm/ID per device role from characterized lookup tables, and size from equations, leaving a few knobs to search and an explainable design. Second, the agent learns the gLayout framework and taught layout practice, and writes a reusable layout generator that closes the layout and extraction loop at designer-approved gates. items.title: Characterizing Performance Tradeoffs in Heterogeneous GPU-Wafer-Scale Accelerator Systems
items.abstract: As AI accelerator architectures become increasingly diverse, integrating different architectures into a unified system is emerging as a new heterogeneous computing paradigm. GPUs and WSEs differ substantially in compute, memory, and communication organization, creating both architectural complementarity and additional overheads, yet how to translate this heterogeneity into practical performance gains remains unclear. To address this gap, we propose a hierarchical benchmarking methodology to characterize GPU--WSE heterogeneous execution and the conditions for exploiting complementarity, together with an analytical performance model that identifies when heterogeneity becomes a bottleneck and when it yields system-level performance gains.

items.title: Colossal magnetoresistance in narrow-gap magnetic semiconductor Eu$_2$CdAs$_2$
items.abstract: Discovering antiferromagnetic materials with a sizable colossal magnetoresistance (CMR) effect and precisely tuning their responses remain significant challenges in materials science. This work reports the synthesis, phase transitions, and magnetotransport properties of the narrow-gap Zintl arsenide Eu$_2$CdAs$_2$. The compound undergoes antiferromagnetic ordering at $T_\mathrm{N} = 9$ K and exhibits semiconducting behavior with a low-temperature activation energy of 3.2 meV, achieving a large CMR effect of $-10^4\%$ at 9 T. Below $T_\mathrm{N}$, a distinct butterfly-shaped magnetoresistance hysteresis emerges without any macroscopic ferromagnetic order, revealing a transport anomaly likely dictated by AFM domain dynamics and/or the formation and percolation of localized magnetic polarons. items.title: Lone-Pair Stereoactivity Overrides Mass Scaling of Thermal Expansion and Heat Conduction in Non-vander Waals Layered Bismuth Oxychalcogenides
items.abstract: Heavier chalcogens are generally expected to soften isostructural semiconductor lattices, raising thermal expansion and lowering thermal conductivity. Layered bismuth oxychalcogenides, Bi2O2X (X = S, Se, Te), are mixed-anion crystals whose covalent slabs and ionic sheets are bound electrostatically rather than by van der Waals forces and whose Bi3+ 6s^2 lone pairs can become stereochemically active. Despite the rapid development of Bi2O2Se for fin and gate-all-around transistors, its fundamental thermal expansion and heat transport mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we show that lone-pair stereoactivity, not chalcogen mass, governs both properties. items.title: Numerical schemes for 1D capacitively coupled plasma fluid simulation
items.abstract: Capacitively coupled plasmas (CCP) are widely used in semiconductor manufacturing, where fluid models provide an efficient approach to the simulation of the low-temperature discharge. The model considered in this work couples the electron and the ion continuity equations, the electron energy equation and the Poisson's equation for the electric potential. We investigate the numerical schemes for the simulation of the 1D-CCP. In particular, a semi-implicit Scharfetter-Gummel (SG) scheme is adopted for the Poisson's equation, while the remaining equations are solved using the implicit SG schemes. The proposed strategy can be naturally extended to the 2D cases. Several alternative schemes are also discussed and tested. items.abstract: Nanophotonic patterning is a promising approach to enhancing light extraction in scintillator materials, with the potential to improve performance in applications such as medical imaging and particle detection. While 2D surface patterns have been successful in improving scintillator performance, the true potential of nanophotonic patterning lies in the bulk, where photons are emitted, transported, and absorbed. Here, we experimentally demonstrate the enhancement and control of scintillation using 2.5D volumetric nanophotonic patterns. Using a direct femtosecond laser writing approach, we nanofabricate square lattices of air holes into the bulk of inorganic scintillators (YAG:Ce and YAG:Yb), achieving nearly subwavelength periods compared to the peak emission wavelength and depths up to hundreds of microns, which fill a large fraction of the full thickness of the bulk. items.abstract: Frontier large language models write correct CUDA kernels for most single-operator benchmark tasks, yet their accuracy collapses on accelerators whose architecture and programming language they have rarely seen. We present a case study of an LLM agent loop built for such accelerators. Our example is the FuriosaAI RNGD NPU, programmed in a recent, sparsely documented Rust DSL, where the loop optimized three Gemma-4-12B decode kernels over 12 days on a shared, scarce device. The loop builds its own target knowledge: it writes and checks a summary of the DSL documentation, measures the chip with microbenchmarks, records compiler-derived legality rules, and revisits this knowledge when the toolchain changes, rechecking rules and measurements where it can. items.abstract: Design-based metrology of academic electron beam lithography (EBL) is bottlenecked by low-throughput imaging. For integrated photonics, where nanometre-scale structural variation can significantly limit device performance, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is the standard tool for critical dimension (CD) metrology, revealing the structure of devices that is not available from optical measurements. The following details a methodology that utilises existing hardware in an academic cleanroom: a GDSII-to-SEM software workflow that converts a facility's superseded pattern generator into a CD-SEM for unattended image acquisition and efficient CD and line edge roughness (LER) extraction. items.title: Coherent control and high purity single-photon emission from telecom quantum dots on metamorphic InGaAs
items.abstract: Semiconductor quantum dots emitting in the telecommunication O- and C-bands are promising candidates as single-photon sources for fiber-based quantum communication. In this work, we show how coherent quasi-resonant and phonon-assisted excitation help reveal the intrinsic optical properties of InAs quantum dots embedded in relaxed InGaAs matrices on top of metamorphic InGaAs layers for achieving emission in the telecom bands. By systematically comparing excitation schemes, we separate excitation-induced effects from intrinsic emitter properties. This allows us to observe linewidths as narrow as 21 $μ$eV, the disappearance of slow decay channels, and single-photon purity reaching second-order autocorrelation values in the order of $10^{-2}$. items.title: A Fast and Memory-Efficient Algorithm for Searching Faint Moving Objects using Synthetic Tracking
items.abstract: Detecting unknown faint moving objects using optical imaging is challenging. Long exposure times are infeasible for such targets, as the resulting image streaking causes a loss of signal-to-noise ratio due to energy dispersal across multiple pixels. To address this, synthetic tracking, a track-before-detect method, replaces long exposures with many short exposures, integrating them in post-processing to recover the moving signal. items.abstract: Functionalising the back-end-of-line (BEOL) of CMOS with emerging materials is a key route to neural network accelerators and neuromorphic systems. In this work, we demonstrate for the first time the integration of 2-terminal ferroelectric synaptic weights in the BEOL of as-delivered commercial 180 nm CMOS dies. A novel material stack is proposed, in which a WOx/[HfO2-ZrO2] bilayer is sandwiched between TiN and Mo electrodes. For devices annealed at 450 °C, programming below 1.8 V is achieved with a cycle-to-cycle variation below 3 %. Synaptic weights annealed at 500 °C exhibit more gradual weight updates, while the tested underlying NMOS transistors remain functional after the complete integration process. The trade-off between thermal budget and on-device training performance is illustrated using hardware-aware neural network simulations.

items.abstract: Spintronic terahertz (THz) emitters based on ferromagnet/heavy-metal bilayers provide an efficient route for generating broadband THz radiation through ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion. items.title: Machine Learning Hamiltonians with Polarizations for Heterogeneous Systems
items.abstract: Machine learning Hamiltonians use local atomic structures to determine local Hamiltonian matrix elements without carrying out self-consistent calculations. They have been used to study large systems and to carry out high-throughput screening for their electronic and optical properties. items.title: Demonstration of high output power (3.75 W/mm) with 31.8% PAE in Ga-Polar AlGaN/GaN HEMTs on sapphire at 94 GHz
items.abstract: In this work, a recessed-gate Ga-polar AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) on sapphire incorporating an AlGaN back-barrier for W-band operation is demonstrated. The device achieves a subthreshold slope of ~130 mV/dec, a peak transconductance of 0.75 S/mm, and an fmax exceeding 240 GHz. Continuous-wave load-pull measurements at 94 GHz show an output power of 3.75 W/mm with a power-added efficiency of 31.8%. This performance significantly exceeds the best previously reported Ga-polar devices on sapphire and approaches that of state-of-the-art Ga-polar devices on SiC, which provides a promising pathway toward high-performance W-band devices.

items.title: Coherent Optical Control of a Single Donor Electron Spin
items.abstract: Coherent spin-photon interfaces are essential for scalable quantum networks, but their realization requires optically bright transitions, long-lived spin coherence, and complete coherent control. However, coherent control of an individual optically active donor spin has remained elusive. Here we demonstrate optical initialization, coherent control, and readout of a single donor-bound electron spin in ZnSe. Using spin-selective donor-bound exciton optical transitions, we initialize the electron spin and directly resolve its spin-relaxation dynamics. items.title: Online Open-World Wafer Defect Discovery using Hyperdimensional Computing
items.abstract: Conventional wafer defect analysis relies on offline, closed-world classifiers that fail to detect novel, unseen defect signatures emerging during continuous semiconductor manufacturing. To address this, we propose WaferHDC, an online open-world wafer defect discovery framework based on hyperdimensional computing (HDC). The memory-centric architecture of WaferHDC enables rapid anomaly detection and grouping of recurring failures into compact hypervector representations. This allows the memory space to dynamically scale with new defect modes without retraining a static classifier or archiving entire raw wafer history. WaferHDC first models normal spatial distributions, then dynamically groups recurring failures into persistent defect memory without labels or predefined class counts. It outperforms the strongest online baseline by 13.3 p.p. in adjusted Rand index and 10.5 p.p. in normalize...
